resources.string: It\'s finally here. Enjoy it with the people you love.
Christmas in less than an hour! 🎄
A new door every day until Christmas Eve.
The calendar opens on 1 December. Come back then!
No ads, no tracking and no data collected. Made with care by Jorge Lillo.
Days or sleeps until Christmas on your home screen.

string-array.name: advent_entries
string-array.item: Write your letter to Santa or the Three Wise Men. Dream big!
\"Jingle Bells\" was the first song ever played in space, on Gemini 6 in December 1965.
Cut out paper snowflakes and stick them on a window.
Christmas trees became fashionable in Britain after an 1848 picture of Queen Victoria and Prince Albert around one.
Movie night: a Christmas film, a blanket and hot chocolate.
Spain\'s Christmas lottery, \"El Gordo\", has been drawn every year since 1812.
Bake Christmas cookies and share a few with a neighbour.
Every snowflake has six arms because ice crystals are hexagonal.
Call or message someone you haven\'t spoken to in a while.
The poinsettia is named after Joel Poinsett, who brought it from Mexico to the United States.
Make a decoration from pine cones, ribbon or anything you find on a walk.
In Catalonia, children feed the \"Caga Tió\", a wooden log that \"gives\" sweets on Christmas.
Donate a toy, a book or some food to someone who needs it.
\"Silent Night\" was first sung on Christmas Eve 1818 in Oberndorf, Austria.
Learn to say it in other languages: Joyeux Noël, Buon Natale, Feliz Natal, Frohe Weihnachten!
In Spain, people eat twelve grapes at midnight on New Year\'s Eve, one per chime.
Go for an evening walk to see the Christmas lights.
Rudolph the red-nosed reindeer was created in 1939 by Robert L. May for a store booklet.
Wrap presents while listening to carols. Tap the music note to play some!
The first tinsel, made in Germany around 1610, was real shredded silver.
Write a thank-you note to someone who made your year better.
NORAD has tracked Santa since 1955, all thanks to a misprinted phone number.
Board game night! Losers make the hot chocolate.
Tonight\'s the night! Leave cookies and milk for Santa, and a carrot for the reindeer. 🎅
